title: The JAMMU AND KASHMIR NATURAL CALAMITIES DESTROYED AREAS IMPROVEMENT ACT, 2011 (1954 A.D.)
full_text: The JAMMU AND KASHMIR NATURAL CALAMITIES DESTROYED AREAS IMPROVEMENT ACT, 2011 (1954 A.D.) Rules Regulations Notifications Orders Circulars Ordinance Statutes SectionsScheduleAnnexureAppendixFormsActdetails Act ID: 201138 Act Number: 38 Enactment Date: 1954-12-24 Act Year: 2011 Short Title: The JAMMU AND KASHMIR NATURAL CALAMITIES DESTROYED AREAS IMPROVEMENT ACT, 2011 (1954 A.D.) Long Title: An Act for improvement of towns, villages or other areas destroyed by natural calamities in the 1Union territory of Jammu and Kashmir. Department: Department of Disaster Management, Relief and Rehabilitation Enforcement Date: 03-02-1955 Type: STATE Location: Jammu and Kashmir TitleFiles TitleFiles TitleFiles TitleFiles Show all section Section 1. Short title, extent, and commencement and application. Section 2. Definitions Section 3. Improvement Scheme. Section 4. Matters that may be dealt with in scheme Section 5. Permission to be taken for construction, etc., after publication of notification under section 3. Section 6. Obligation on owners to comply with scheme after sanction. Section 7. Order of demolition of buildings. Section 7-A. Penalties Section 8. Modification of the Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act. Section 9. Notification under section 3 to have effect as declaration under sections 11 and 19 of the Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act. Section 10. Sections 26, 27 and 28 of the Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act superseded. Section 11. Power of Government to make rules. Section 11-A. Sanction of prosecution. Section 11-B. Protection of action taken in good faith. Section 12. Validity of action taken by the Government or by officers or authorities under the order of the Government in making improvements of towns of Anantnag, Shopian and Baramulla.
